platformAuthority.ratifies: TASK-R2-O1 scope.platformDecision (2026-09-19), which recorded the same answer and left it unenforced.
evidence: 18 of 18 jobs across the 8 files in .github/workflows/ are `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`. No Windows or macOS runner is configured anywhere in this repository.

At the decision, 34 of the 58 accepted baselines carried the `-chromium-linux` suffix (gallery 16, theme-recipe 18) and the 24 per-component pilot images were `-chromium-win32`. Since the 2026-09-26 recapture all 58 are `-chromium-linux`.

Playwright writes `{arg}-{project}-{platform}.png`, so a linux image and a win32 image are different files and are never compared. The suffix is the path the comparison resolves, not editable metadata.
platformAuthority.rationale: The authoritative platform is the one the gate runs on. Only linux has a runner, and the majority of the committed evidence is already linux. Font rasterisation, subpixel antialiasing and scrollbar metrics differ enough between platforms that a cross-platform comparison is a diff storm, not a signal — so exactly one platform is authoritative and every other platform refuses rather than diffing.
platformAuthority.enforcement: e2e/visual/platform.ts compares process.platform against this value for every lane whose role is `gate`, before a browser is launched. `yarn visual:platform` is the same check as a standalone preflight, wired as the first step of `test:e2e:visual` and `test:e2e:visual:pilot`.
platformAuthority.thisIsNotTheAuthoritativePlatform: win32 — the machine this decision was recorded on. The refusal path was proved here; see docs/program-2026-09-22-architecture/reports/TASK-S1-O3-handoff.md.

platformDecision.state: EXECUTED 2026-09-26 (DZUP-UI-VISUAL-LANE-CONTAINER-20260926-R1): the owner picked O6-D2 option b, and every per-component baseline was re-captured on linux inside the pinned CI image mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble@sha256:5b8f294aff9041b7191c34a4bab3ac270157a28774d4b0660e9743297b697e48 and accepted one snapshot per invocation. The 24 win32 images are retired (in git history before this commit).
platformDecision.rationale: The authoritative platform is the one the gate runs on, and every job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (13 of 13) is `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`. A baseline is platform-locked by construction: Playwright writes `{arg}-{project}-{platform}.png`, so a win32 image and a linux image are different files and are never compared. A ledger that gates on win32 therefore gates on a platform no runner has, which is precisely why the per-component lane is developer-local evidence and not a CI gate. So: `linux` is the target, and it is recorded here rather than written into `platform`, because writing it would make this ledger claim 58 baselines that do not exist and `yarn validate:visual-baselines` would fail on 58 `missing` records. `platform` and the committed images agree today (both win32) and that agreement is the thing the gate checks; the disagreement that matters is between `platform` and `ciPlatform`, and it is now a decision with a date rather than a sentence in a note.
platformDecision.ownerAction: Done for the buttons pilot and its four fixtures. Widening scope.families is still one visual:accept per snapshot, inside the pinned image, and is the owner's act per family (TASK-R2-O6 waves 0-4).
platformDecision.consumes: TASK-R2-O6 (visual-regression rollout + CI gate) takes this as its input.
platformDecision.verifiedOn: win32, 2026-09-19, at 2d51eec + a 420-path dirty worktree: `yarn test:e2e:visual:pilot` and `yarn validate:visual-baselines` - see docs/program-2026-09-04/reports/TASK-R2-O1-handoff.md.

scope.note: TASK-N1-O6 pilot. Coverage is declared per FAMILY and joined against e2e/matrix/targets.generated.ts, so a component added to a covered family is covered without editing this file. Components outside these families read `not-covered` in the capability matrix - an explicit state, never `unknown`. PLATFORM: baselines are platform-locked by construction - Playwright writes `{arg}-{project}-{platform}.png`, so a linux baseline and a win32 baseline are different files and are never compared to each other. `platform` is the one this ledger gates on; `ciPlatform` is what .github/workflows/ci.yml runs. They AGREE since 2026-09-26: every baseline is linux, captured in the pinned Playwright image the CI `visual` job runs in (a baseline is evidence only in the environment it was captured in; two apt font packages changed 20 of 24 images in TASK-R2-O6 probe B).

lanes.scope: 8 demo screens × light/dark — "does the composition still look right".
lanes.excludes: Says nothing about WHICH component moved when a screen changes. That is the per-component lane.
Two screens only; a provider regression on a screen outside those two is invisible here.

lanes.scope: Every component in an opted-in family (today: buttons → 8 components) × light/dark, plus 4 declared stress fixtures. maxDiffPixels: 0.
lanes.excludes: Every family outside scope.families reads `not-covered` in the capability matrix — 136 of 144 components today. LTR only; one viewport; chromium only.
lanes.requires: A built apps/storybook/storybook-static. Does NOT need DZUP_GALLERY=1.
lanes.promoted: Promoted 2026-10-01 at the merge of origin/main: upstream recaptured all 24 images inside the pinned Playwright image on 2026-09-26 (owner decision O6-D2 b, accepted on the owner's behalf), deleting the win32 set, so capturedOn is linux and the lane gates like the other two.
